task:
Something terrible happened. Some time after you blew up the ranger's ship, a different ship flew by and picked up the ranger, who managed to seal his spacesuit before his ship was destroyed. He developed a severe case of frostbite during his stay in outer space, but ultimately survived. Now he is undergoing therapy in a specialized hospital on planet <ToPlanet>.
As you can understand, we can't consider your mission as being accomplished while <Ship> is still alive. So it's in your best interest to quickly get to star system <ToStar>, infiltrate the hospital, and finish off that tenacious ranger. True, there is one teensy weensy problem with this. Due to the severe climate and freezing temperatures, the place is more like a fortress than a hospital, so you won't be able to get in with a weapon. But don't worry. You don't have to smother him with a pillow or pinch the hoses of his breathing machine. As far as we have been able to determine, the institution's air supply system is completely self-contained and does not rely on external sources. Your mission is to penetrate this system and break it. Then the ranger will either freeze to death or suffocate, in either order. Of course, all the other patients will perish, and the hospital staff, but that's nothing you need to worry about, right?
So, your mission is to take care of the ranger once and for all before <Date>. You can consider that promotion as already in your pocket.
success: Well, very good, <Player>. You're a real cut-throat. Did you catch the meaning in that? Cut-throat! Now you're the terror of the galaxy and everyone must fear you. Except pirates who know more than you, of course. Ha! Carry on advancing the work of pirate society: cheat, rob, kill. Your next promotion will be unstoppable.
loc.1.0:
You descended and entered planet <ToPlanet>'s atmosphere. A powerful wind immediately began to blow your ship about, like underwear drying on the line. Who knows where you got that analogy from, because nobody is drying anything for as far as the eye can see. Gloomy black cliffs and icy hummocks didn't foreshadow anything good for you, so you prudently climbed a bit higher. Indeed, if you were to crash your chances of survival would be very small, considering the fact that the planet's atmosphere, while at least it has one, isn't suitable for breathing. In theory, this is the very thing that makes feasible your plan to eliminate the unfortunate surviving ranger.

You decided to review in your mind the sequence of actions you need to take:
First, you need to confirm that the ranger is in the hospital. And to do that you need to see him with your own eyes. Second, as soon as you determine your victim is in place, you need to work your way to the service level, find the ventilation system, and release all of the hospital's air into the atmosphere. If everybody dies, the incident will probably be written off as an accident, because no witnesses to your activities will remain.

Finally, the imposing, windowless, low hospital building appeared up ahead. You carefully flew into the main hangar and landed on a platform illuminated by red lights, as directed by the air traffic controller. Killing the engine, you noticed that the hangar was nearly empty, except for a faeyan ship parked in the far corner with no owner in sight. Well, that's probably for the best, considering what you have to do.
As you left the cabin, you automatically shoved your trusty blaster under your belt.

You had just gotten out of the ship when a small service droid flew up to scan you, a measure designed to prevent harmful bacteria and viruses from entering the hospital. It winked at you in a friendly way with its various lights and squeaked something, probably a greeting.
loc.2.0: You demonstratively raised your hands upward, which the approaching droid correctly took as a call to action. It began to circle around you, screeching and brandishing scanner appendages. After it stopped fussing, it froze in place to process the information. You had already begun to relax when it squawked sharply and a holographic sign appeared over its head: "Please leave your weapon on your ship".
loc.3.0:
You put your plan into action and watched as the poor droid peeped and whirled away. But it cost you to take a step forward, as three armored guards appeared with automatic blasters in their hands. Their manly chins didn't foreshadow anything good for you.
"You declined to be scanned, sir." said one of them. "Please explain the reason for this violation of hospital policy".
loc.4.0: "No problem, sir." said the guard. "We'll do an examination instead of a scan". Refusing to submit to scanning on religious grounds really isn't that uncommon, so a backup plan has been developed. Come with us to the procedure room.
loc.5.0:
They undressed you and subjected you a most humiliating examination, clearly a form of punishment for failing to submit to the established rules. But you proudly endured the examination process and didn't allow yourself to be broken - you even repeated maloq tongue-twisters after one of the guards.
Finally, they told you to get dressed and expressed the hope that you would enjoy your stay. And they deprived you of your trusty blaster.
loc.6.0: "No problem, sir." said the guard. "We'll perform an examination instead of a scan". Refusing to submit to scanning due to droidophobia really isn't that uncommon, so a backup plan has been developed. Come with us to the procedure room.
loc.7.0:
"Okay, sir. It's your right." said the guard without changing his facial expression. "Sometimes people don't submit to us either, so a procedure has been developed. 
Before you could even open your mouth, the dashing young men seized you, threw you into the cabin of your ship, and started the autopilot. 
"Don't return until you've changed your mind about being scanned," warned a guard as he slammed the cabin window down in front of your nose.
After a moment your ship started and flew out of the hangar at top speed.
loc.8.0: You pulled your weapon out of the holster and shoved it under the pilot's seat. Then you climbed out of the ship again and looked around. Apparently, everybody lost interest in you, so it was worth it to disarm yourself. You had the crazy idea of surreptitiously getting your weapon back, but you quickly realized that this would be detected immediately after you noticed a surveillance camera directly over your head, vigilantly watching your every move.
loc.9.0: You ignored the droid's request and stepped forward. But you had barely twitched when an alarm started to screech throughout the entire hangar and a turret hidden in the ceiling fired a shock charge at you.

"You are in the room of the doctor on duty at the hospital," he said, "How do you feel?"

The supplies disappointed you. All you could find were several uniforms, pistols, and oxygen masks. You didn't see any rounds for the gun.
loc.49.0: You are inside a small dirty room. Directly in the center is a table. A few workers are sitting behind it, having a lively conversation about something and throwing dice onto the table from time to time. One more door is visible on the far wall.
loc.49.1: You are inside a small dirty room. Directly in the center is a table. Several overturned chairs are lying on the floor around it, along with the bodies of workers who died from a lack of oxygen. There's nothing more to do here.
loc.50.0:
You are inside a restroom divided into five compartments - one for each race of the Coalition. The interior is clean, bright, and smells of some sort of disinfectant.
A plumber is tinkering in one of the stalls, whistling happily.
loc.50.1: You went into one of the stalls, took care of business, made a plan, and then stood in front of the mirror for some time, examining your reflection for blemishes.
loc.50.2: You are inside a restroom divided into five compartments - one for each race of the Coalition. The interior is clean, bright, and you can't smell a thing through your mask. A plumber's corpse is lying in one of the stalls. Apparently, he had been doing some repairs.
loc.50.3:
You approached one of the sinks and turned the knob to turn on the water. To your surprise, instead of water coming from the faucet, some sort of rumbling could be heard. You turned the knob once again after hearing another series of unearthly sounds. You had already decided to spit and walk away from the sink when, suddenly, a powerful stream of icy water blasted out of the faucet. Your scream could probably be heard everywhere, all the way up to the fourth floor.
"Hey, pal. It's not your lucky day," remarked the plumber crawling out of the stall, "You picked the only bad faucet".
"Couldn't you have put a sign on it?" you exploded.
"Seemed like everybody already knew," said the worker, shrugging his shoulders apathetically.
"Well, what am I going to do now?"
"Hmm..." thought the plumber out loud, "Well, I can give you my spare coveralls - they're clean. More or less."
loc.50.4:
You took the plumber's clothing, went into one of the stalls, and changed your clothes. So what if nobody will be able to distinguish you from a worker? Now you're dry and comfortable.
Almost automatically, you felt the pockets of your new getup and unexpectedly discovered a magnetic key card inside. Because its owner had just gone off somewhere, you decided that it would yet be of use to you personally.
loc.51.0: You are inside an auxiliary room. It's dark and something is dripping on one of the corners. The shelves along the walls are covered with uninteresting odds and ends.
loc.51.1: You took a light from the shelf, picking out the one that looked the newest.
loc.52.0:
"What do you need, pal?" asked one of the workers.
"Oh, nothing. I'm already leaving," you said haltingly and left.
loc.52.1:
You approached the table.
"What do you want, doc?" inquired one of the workers.
loc.52.2:
"Hey, man!" the workers said in greeting.
Apparently, not one of them suspected that you weren't their colleague at all.
loc.52.3: "Do you need something?" asked one of the workers, quickly hiding the dice in his pocket.
loc.53.0:
"Hey, guys. You've been summoned to waiting room. They need something moved there."
"All of us together?"
"Yeah, there's some sort of heavy apparatus," you lied without blinking.
The workers exchanged glances helplessly, got up from their seats, and left the room, mumbling and complaining about back pain.
loc.53.1:
"Say! There's our man!" the workers rejoiced, "Take the dice!
"What are we playing for?" you asked, just in case.
"Just for fun. Gambling is strictly forbidden here. You keep that in mind if something happens."
loc.53.2:
"Attaboy!" you exclaimed in praise, "Let's play again - what else is there to do?!" 
"By the way," interjected one of them, "fellas, did you hear that we have a new nurse at the entrance? Such a cutie. She loves chocolate."
The rest of the workers nodded their heads in agreement.
loc.53.3:
"All right!" rejoiced the workers, "Let's play again - what else is there to do?!" 
"By the way," interjected one of them, "this new security chief, Major Ugrom. He's occasionally a jerk, but at least he's a maloq."
The rest of the workers nodded their heads in agreement.
loc.53.4:
"Excellent!" nodded the workers, "Let's play again - what else is there to do?!" 
"By the way," interjected one of them, "in this ward, where the frostbitten ranger is, the ventilation isn't working well. I hope they send someone from a different shift to do the repairs, otherwise they'll get lazy.
The rest of the workers nodded their heads in agreement.
loc.53.5: "Nah, excuse me, pal. Time for a smoke," responded the workers.

loc.59.0:
As soon as the workers left the room you immediately abandoned your feigned leisurely attitude and began looking around the room for something useful. Unfortunately, other than the dice on the table and various posters of beautiful peleng women, you couldn't find anything else in the room. Then you went into the next room, which turned out to be a small locker room.
You surveyed the room and discovered that one of the lockers was open. There were some coveralls inside.
The workers will be back soon and be very angry, so you need to hurry.
loc.60.0:
Before the workers returned, you managed to pull on the coveralls, fasten all the buttons and zippers, and hide the doctor's coat in the locker. Now you must get out of the room as quickly as possible, otherwise your behavior will look highly suspicious.
You discovered a key card in one of the pockets of the coveralls. It will probably come in handy.
loc.61.0:
"Listen. I need to ask for a favor. Do you know how to replace a light bulb?!" asked the nurse.
You instantly began swearing that you were screwing in light bulbs almost from your mother's womb.
"Excellent!" she said, beaming. "Please swing by the second level and replace the light in the general ward! You can get a new bulb from Kuzmich in the office!"
Her ability to speak in exclamations decidedly touched something in your soul.
loc.61.1: "Sorry, that's confidential information!" answered the nurse, "We don't give out information about our patients!!"
loc.61.2:
Tears suddenly flooded from the nurse's eyes. You recoiled in fright.
"What a...sorry, what a sad story!" said the nurse, sniffling. "But, unfortunately, we don't release information about patients undergoing treatment! Even about best friends!
loc.61.3:
The nurse remained silent with a gaping mouth, looking at you like people usually look at a volcano erupting unexpectedly somewhere in a garden of faryuks. Apparently, she isn't given many compliments here.
"Would you like leave a written request...?!" she asked, finally.
loc.61.4:
"DEAR ME!!" You were nearly swept away by the sonic boom. "What's this? For me?! Thank you! Thank you!! Thank you!!!"
The nurse snatched the chocolate from your hands and you realized that now she would do anything to help you.
loc.61.5:
"I simply adore men in military uniform!" the nurse blurted, devouring you with her eyes.
"Uh...I'll go check," you mumbled, slowly backing away from the counter.
You don't have time to be distracted from your mission!
loc.63.0:
"I'm Kuzmich," said one of the workers, raising his hand. He had a big red beard. "Remember that. It's not difficult."
The rest of the workers laughed heartily.
"Did you need something?"
loc.63.1: "There's the piece of crap. It's gone and burned out again. There ain't never gonna be enough light bulbs for this ward. You head on down to the utility room at the end of the corridor. There's a light bulb there on the shelf to the right - and there's a ladder in the ward. You got any more questions?"
loc.63.2: "Yeah, impress everyone with your work," frowned the worker, "Get lost, comedian."
loc.67.0: There are exactly three private wards on the level. An enormous maloq guard is keeping watch over the entrance to the second ward. His appearance doesn't foreshadow anything good. The doors of the other wards have been flung wide open. Nobody is inside.
loc.68.0:
"Not without a pass!" growled the guard in a deep voice when you approached.
You tried to shove him, but apparently he didn't even notice. Even a kick in the knee, which you had decided on in utter despair, didn't help the situation at all.
loc.68.1:
"Not without a pass!" growled the guard in a deep voice when you approached.
"How fortunate that I have one," you replied and waved the pass clenched in your hand.
The nearsighted guard read what was written on it, wrinkling and moving his lips. Then he snarled with discontent and stepped to the side, freeing the way.
loc.68.2:
"Not without a pass!" growled the guard in a deep voice when you approached.
"Uh, I've come to fix the ventilation," you replied peaceably.
"Ventilation?" The guard's forehead crumpled up.
"Yessir. They said it's broken."
"Okay, fine," said the guard, giving up. "Go ahead."
Fortunately, he didn't even ask where your tools were.
loc.68.3:
"Doc," growled the guard as you walked past.
"Yes?" you asked, growing cold with the thought that you had been found out.
"Do you have any of those vitamins that taste good?" asked the guard unexpectedly.
"Er...no, I'm afraid I don't."
"Bummer..." boomed the guard and turned his attention away from you.
loc.68.4: The guard gave you a watchful glance as you approached the door, but he didn't say anything as he stepped to the side to free the way.
loc.68.5:
"Not without a pass!" growled the guard in a deep voice when you approached.
In reply, you offered him the bar of chocolate you had procured at the buffet. Dumbfounded, you watched as the guard's sour face spread into a smile.
"Gee, thanks!" he bellowed, snatching the confection from your hands and adding, "You can go in."
loc.69.0:
You are inside a small, windowless room. Directly opposite from the door is a bed with somebody completed wrapped in bandages lying in it. Various tubes and wires protrude from the bandages and lead to a complicated apparatus at the head of the bed.
You took a step forward and read the sign on the end of the bed. This was indeed your enemy who had survived. You involuntarily impressed by his struggle to live. 
Well, once you determined that your victim is in place, the only thing left to do is finish him off. Or would it be better to have pity on the innocent patients and think up something new? You have a difficult decision to make.
loc.70.0:
You couldn't resist and, despite the plan which had been painstakingly developed for the murder, you decided to end the problem right there. 
Carefully extracting the pillow from underneath the bandaged head, you pressed it tightly over the ranger's face. A moment passed. Then another, and another. You held the pillow solidly in place. Finally, your victim began to stir, sensing the lack of air, and the apparatus at the head of the bed suddenly began beeping intensely. 
The guard immediately burst into the ward, followed by a doctor. The maloq threw you to the side of the bed with a powerful blow, which brought your infamous activity to an end.
loc.71.0: You are in the waiting room. It is a small room without windows. Against one wall is a solitary sunken couch, and on the opposite wall is a door labeled "Weapon room". The door to the security chief's office is right in the middle, opposite the entrance. On the door is written "Security Chief - Major Ugrom".
loc.73.0:
You entered the doorway and noticed that you were in a ridiculously small room, in which two guards were discontentedly staring at you, having been interrupted from browsing the magazine of "Ranger Pride".
"What do you want?" asked one of the guards.
loc.74.0: The escape hatch is completely blocked. Dozens of warning signs have been stuck all over it. Next to the hatch is a small panel with a magnetic key-card reader.
loc.74.1: You inserted the key card into the panel. There was a quiet beep and a red light started flashing on the panel.
loc.74.2: You inserted the key card into the panel. There was a quiet beep and the escape hatch opened.
loc.75.0: You cautiously crept up to the door and put one ear to it, trying to hear sounds from the other side. That ended when you got whacked in the ear by the door as it opened.
loc.75.1: You watched the door closely. It's closed, but on the wall nearby there's a small panel to unlock it using a magnetic key card.
loc.75.2: You put the key card into the reader on the panel. There was a quiet beep, but the door didn't open and a red light started flashing on the panel.
loc.75.3: The list of useful things in the weapon room was disappointing. All you could find were several uniforms, pistols, and oxygen masks. No ammunition anywhere.
loc.77.0:
"Hey, hey! Who do we have here?" barked the stern voice of Major Ugrom over your head. "Are you spying on me, kid?"
"No, no!" you screamed as the major's steel fingers dug into your shoulder. "I, uh...I'm just passing by! I'm not a spy!"
"I'm going to tear you in half and eat you!" the major roared, leaning toward your pale face.
You had already prepared yourself to die, but the major couldn't contain himself any longer and started laughing.
"Relax. I'm just kidding. Better go to the guardroom and call one of the boys."
The major immediately lost interest in you and disappeared into his office.
loc.77.1:
"Oh, excuse me," you heard Major Ugrom say, "I didn't know you were here."
"No problem. Everything is okay, sir," you replied, holding your bruised ear.
"Was there something you need?" asked the major, holding the door open.
"No, sir. Sorry to disturb you!" you bellowed, circling around and quickly marching out of the waiting room.
loc.79.0: You are inside a ventilation shaft. It's so big you can stand up straight. There are technical signs on the sides of the tunnel, but they don't mean a thing to you. The dim light barely illuminates a web of small tubes and electric cables on the walls. If this system runs through the entire building, then it looks like you'll be able to get anywhere you want.
loc.80.0: You walked about twenty steps and saw an escape hatch in the solid wall of the tunnel.
loc.81.0: Before you had walked twenty steps down the tunnel, you nearly toppled into a vertical shaft that lead somewhere below, probably to the second level. Looks like you won't have any luck here.
loc.82.0:
You walked for quite a long time until the tunnel was obstructed by the blades of an enormous fan. 
It is running and there's no way to get around it. Behind the fan there is a vertical shaft which has been conveniently equipped with rungs to climb up or down.
loc.83.0: The hatch opened without giving you any trouble, and you climbed into a dimly lit room.
loc.84.0:
You are in the room with the control panel for the air circulation system. It seems this is precisely where you needed to come to complete your dark deed.
A large portion of the room is occupied by various high-tech devices that flash and twinkle with all sorts of lights. And in the farthest part of the room is the main control panel for the whole system. That's what you'll be able to use to disable the ventilation system and destroy the ranger along with every other humanoid in the hospital.
An escape hatch covered with warning signs is built into the far wall.
loc.85.0:
"What, only one?" asked the second, hiding the magazine in his pocket.
"The other guy will be here soon. He couldn't hold it any longer..." you said, making a face. The guards understood and laughed.
"Well, have fun!" they said as they left the room.
You weren't listening, because you had noticed that there was another door in the room. Large letters overhead read: "Air Circulation System".
loc.85.1:
"He never knows when to stop..." said one of the guards, putting the magazine into his pocket.
They got up from their seats and left, leaving you there in disbelief at your good fortune. Not only because the guards has left you alone, but more importantly, because you noticed another door in the room. Large letters overhead read: "Air Circulation System".
loc.86.0:
For a couple of minutes you pecked at the control panel with your fingers and came to the conclusion that you were in a position to disable the air supply system and release all of the air. However, all four levels of the hospital were controlled by separate units, so you can only release the air in turns, one level after another. Of course, you won't be able to release all of the air in a minute. Therefore, you need everyone to leave you alone for at least twenty minutes.

Just one question remains: is destroying the life of a single ranger worth the lives of several hundred citizens of the Coalition? And wouldn't it be better for you to think of some other resolution to the situation without resorting to mass genocide even though it would guarantee successful completion of your mission?
loc.86.1: After dragging the heavy operator's chair to the door, you inserted it instead of the crosspiece between the two tubes on either side of the door. This won't hold the guards for long, but it will give you a headstart of a couple of minutes.
loc.86.2: You removed the oxygen mask from your belt and put it on. This was a wise decision, considering that you will be without air just like everyone else who doesn't manage to put on a mask.
loc.86.3: You rummaged about the room, but you didn't find anything useful other than an emergency cabinet in which a single protective mask was hanging.
loc.86.4: You rummaged about the room, but you didn't find anything useful. Then you returned to the control panel.
loc.94.0: You opened the door and went through it, but somebody immediately attacked you, knocking you off your feet. Dazed, you jumped back and observed that one of the guards had also managed to put on a mask. And now he wanted to rip you to pieces. You had not doubt he would success in doing this, because he was almost twice as muscular as you.
loc.95.0: You caught the guard with a fake move and slipped off his mask. He fell to your feet, gasping, but you stepped over his body and moved toward the elevator.
loc.95.1:
You whipped out the pistol and walloped the guard across his mask. The glass cracked and the air began bleeding out. The guard immediately lost interest in your, because his mask was no longer supplying oxygen. He began to gasp. But you didn't finish him off, since he only had a couple of minutes left anyway.
Leaving your enemy, you returned to the main corridor and headed for the elevator.
loc.96.0: Trying to overcome him in a fair fight was a big mistake. The guard easily caught you with a counter-maneuver and ripped your mask off. You hardly sensed that you had nothing to breath as all of your zeal for battle disappeared in an instant. The guard obviously did not intend to settle down. He laid into your ribs, causing your to exhale your last measly puffs of air. You began to suffocate. This was an ignominious death, though you did accomplish your mission.
loc.96.1: You tried to catch your enemy with a counter-maneuver in order to rip off his mask, but he guessed your plan while you were still formulating it. Evading your hands, he responded by elbowing you in the ribs, and when you submissively folded up from the pain he ripped your protective mask off. You hardly sensed that you had nothing to breath as all of your zeal for battle disappeared in an instant. The guard obviously did not intend to settle down. He again laid into your ribs, causing your to exhale your last measly puffs of air. You began to suffocate. This was an ignominious death, though you did accomplish your mission.
loc.98.0:
You blocked the entrance behind you to prevent the guards from pursuing you. Then you looked around in amazement as you entered the hall, which was covered with soft, fluffy carpets. The office was an enormous round dome made of glass framed in strips of plastic. The transparent walls open to a stunning view of mountain peaks capped with snow. In large vats that stand along the edges of the office, fantastic tropical plants grow, seemingly laughing at the cold on the other side of the glass.
Distracted by your study of the surrounding view, you entirely lost sight of the fact that the hospital chief was somewhere in the office - and probably very surprised by your sudden appearance, gun in hand. So when...
"Halt!" sounded a hoarse, weak voice. 
You turned your head around and observed a large work desk in the far part of the room. A feeble, old gaalian was hiding behind it.
loc.98.1:
You went into the corridor and followed the maloq into the elevator. He pressed the button for the fourth floor. 
The look on the faces of the guards who saw you emerge from the elevator together with Ugrom was compensation enough for all the unpleasantness you had endured on this rough day.
Passing through a small corridor, you followed the major through the open door and stopped in amazement after seeing what the office of a hospital chief looks like. The room turned out to be an enormous round dome made of glass framed in strips of plastic. The transparent walls open to a stunning view of mountain peaks capped with snow. In large vats that stand along the edges of the office, fantastic tropical plants grow, seemingly laughing at the cold on the other side of the glass.
Among all this splendor, you didn't immediately see the massive writing table and the elderly gaalian sitting behind it.
loc.100.0: A turnstile rises directly in front of the elevator, blocking the way. Apparently, only those whose work duties require it can get through on this floor. A small image of a magnetic card is flashing on the terminal near the turnstile.
loc.100.1: You inserted the card into the terminal. There was a quiet beep and a red light began flashing on the panel. This card won't work.
loc.100.2: You inserted the card into the terminal. There was a quiet beep and the terminal's gates moved apart with a hiss. The way onto the floor is clear.
loc.100.3:
Using your priceless experience in riding on public transportation during your youth, you raced forward, pulled off a triple toe loop with a flip, and were already on the other side in an instant. 
Before you managed to get any applause a vicious guard hung over you, grabbed you by the ear, and returned you to the elevator. Then he pointed at the video camera over the turnstile, threatened you with his finger, and left.
loc.102.0:
You went into the corridor after the guard, passed through the turnstile, and found yourself near the elevator.
"Have a good day," said the guard with a salute as he left.
loc.102.1:
You entered the corridor where the guard was waiting for you.
"Finally..." he said, "Did you fall asleep in there or what?"
He took you to the elevator through a turnstile that didn't stop anyone from passing.
"Have a good day," said the guard with a salute as he left.

So you have four levels where you need to pump out the air. What should we start with?
It would be best to start with the second level to finish off the ranger as quickly as possible. But, on the other hand, if you start releasing the air from the other levels, then the guards will put an end to your privacy in this room.
The only thing left to do is to decide which button to press...
loc.105.0:
Accompanied by the buzz of the exhaust pumps and the sound of the emergency alarm, the first floor of the hospital was completely deprived of any air suitable for breathing. The attractive nurse at the registration counter, the workers in the "Bureau", the personnel in the hangar - they all became just a part of a long, sordid story. 
The guards are beating with their fists on the door behind you, trying in vain to get back into the room. For the time being, the chair is holding like a champ.
What level will be next?
loc.105.1:
The floor beneath your feet began to shudder slightly when the powerful air pumps started running to release the oxygen from the second level. All the while, you stubbornly chased out of your head images of how the unfortunate hospital patients on the level below are being tortured with the lack of air, convulsing as they try to inhale the last miserable whiffs of oxygen that remain. At least the ranger in the second private ward is probably already dead, which means that you can consider your primary mission accomplished. 
The guards are beating with their fists on the door behind you, trying in vain to get back into the room. For the time being, the chair is holding like a champ.
loc.105.2:

You mentally praised your forethought. If not for your protective mask, you would have begun suffocating from a lack of air.
You can only hope that nobody else managed to do the same.

"So what? He's just an ordinary worker..."

You stopped eavesdropping so as not to arouse suspicion.

loc.109.0: You barely escaped from the ward with the help of the bodybuilder orderly, losing a patch of hair in the process and receiving a lovely shiner. And only half of your doctor's coat remained. Being a doctor is hard work!

loc.111.1: The floor beneath your feet began to shudder slightly when the powerful air pumps started running to release the oxygen from the second level. All the while, you stubbornly chased out of your head images of how the unfortunate hospital patients on the level below are being tortured with the lack of air, convulsing as they try to inhale the last miserable whiffs of oxygen that remain. At least the ranger in the second private ward is also dead, which means that you can consider your primary mission accomplished.
loc.111.2:
You had just activated the evacuation of air on the third level - the level you are on - when the air pumps, located in the very room you are in, began whistling as they sucked out the air. They were so powerful that everything around you began to shake, the metal joints of the tubes thundered, and behind the wall in the ventilation tunnel, it sounded like an enormous vortex had formed. You mentally praised your forethought. If not for your protective mask, you would have begun suffocating from a lack of air.
You can only hope that nobody else managed to do the same.

You quietly approached the registration counter, leaned over it, and looked down. You saw the tear-stained eyes of the nurse whose beauty nearly ruined your protective mask.
"Oh, it's you!" she said with a sigh of relief, "I'm scared to death! When everybody began to fall down...And this air!" It's so good that this week I wasn't too lazy to bring my mask to my station and keep it the desk! I thought I was the only one who survived!! I'm so glad that you're still alive too...!"

Regarding her last statement, you wouldn't have been afraid to disagree even for a thousand credits. If you hadn't found her, she may have had a chance of surviving, but now, when she knows your face...
loc.115.1:
You extended your hand to the nurse as if you were going to help her get up, but as soon as she moved forward, you bent down and yanked the mask off her face. She instinctively began to scream in fright, but the lack of oxygen in the air quickly forced her to calm down. She clutched her throat with her hands, but you turned away so as to not see her puzzled expression.
At the moment, more than anything else, you wished that this had never happened. In a different life you might have met under entirely different circumstances, but there's nothing you can do to save her now. It's too bad that you can't return to the past and make a different choice. After all, all the pirate plans to conquer the galaxy aren't worth the death of this girl alone.

Only then did you steer the ship from the hangar into the planet's frosty atmosphere, which had involuntarily become your accomplice in this sordid murder.

Even if you are able to deal with them, this will be an unnecessary waste of time and oxygen. Instead, you could try to work your way back to the landing hangar through the ventilation system's tunnels.

"Don't worry! I won't hurt you!" you yelled, throwing aside your pistol, which hit one of the tables and broke something fragile and made out of glass. 
Now it would be great if this retired gaalian wouldn't hurt you either.
loc.127.1:
"Hey, old man. I come in peace!" you bellowed, raising your weapon and pointing it at the gaalian.
"Oh, Universe..." whispered the gaalian, letting his weapon fall. "Please spare me!"
"Hey, it's not even loaded!" you yelled, throwing the pistol on the floor. "Don't you understand? I'm here to tell you that I just saved you all from death. And you're pointing a gun at me?! How rude!"
"Excuse me, what do you mean?"
loc.128.0:
You whipped out the pistol that you had previously borrowed from the weapon room and pointed it in the direction of the guards. They didn't even manage to raise their weapons in response.
"Hands up!" you shouted. "Higher!"
The guards hesitated for a moment, but then complied.
"Throw down your weapons!" you continued, "And open the door."
When your request was fulfilled, you slowly moved toward the door, keeping the barrel of your gun pointed right at the guards. When there was less than two meters between you, one of the guards lost it and lunged at you. You were distracted for a moment and he managed to plow into you, knocking you off your feet. The pistol flew out of your hands and the second guard instantly jumped to assist his colleague. Together, they subdued you and dragged you to the security chief to figure out who you are and what they should do with you.
loc.129.0:
You descended to the floor below and asked the first guard you met to take you to the security chief. He gave you suspicious look, but escorted you right up to the office. 
The major was there, sitting behind his enormous table and reading some papers. He tore himself away from them to look at you when you came in.
"What do you need?" he asked directly, without showing any undue respect.
loc.129.1:
Accompanied by the guards, you descended to the floor below, passed through the turnstile, and turned into the door on the right wall of the corridor.
The major was there, sitting behind his enormous table and reading some papers. He tore himself away from them to see what was happening when the guards literally dragged you into his office.
"What do you need?" he asked directly, without showing any undue respect.
"He was trying to break into the hospital chief's office," reported one of the guards. "And threatened us with a weapon."
The major took the pistol that you used to threaten the guards, looked at its identification number, and extracted and checked the clip, which was empty, as you expected.
"Find out whose this is," he said, throwing the weapon to the guards. "And then file a report. And who the heck is at your post if you're both here?"
Embarrassed, the guards immediately left the room, and the maloq turned his eyes to you.
"For some reason I knew you were going to be trouble from the moment you flew into our hangar. What do you have to say for yourself?"
loc.130.0:
"I'll only speak to the hospital chief about that! you declared firmly.
"What? Something you don't like about me?" asked Ugrom with a grave smile. "Don't I have ears?"
"Sorry, but the information is just too important," you replied.
"Even more important still is that I have reason to know immediately. What? You think the hospital chief is in charge here? He's just a figurehead who smiles for the camera and signs documents. I'm the one who decides everything. That's my job. So you can either tell me what's going on, or we'll throw you out before you can say, 'There's been a mistake!', understand?!"
loc.130.1:
"I have information for the hospital chief, but your people won't let me reach him!"
"Just as they should," shrugged Major Ugrom. "There's nothing for an outsider to do in his office. What? You think the hospital chief is in charge here? He's just a figurehead who smiles for the camera and signs documents. I'm the one who decides everything. That's my job. So you can either tell me what's going on, or we'll throw you out before you can say, 'There's been a mistake!', understand?!"
loc.130.2:
"Very interesting... replied the major. "Continue."
You exhaled deeply and, having made up your mind, you told the major about the assignment you had received at the pirate base, about the ranger, about the ventilation system - in short, about everything. The major sat silently for a while after you finished, but you had hardly opened your mouth again when he got up from his seat.
"Let's go," he said, waving his hand and moving toward the door.
loc.131.0:
"Okay, as you wish," responded the major indifferently.
He pressed a communication button and called in a couple of even stronger guards.
"Throw him out of the hospital," he ordered when the guards appeared in his office.
You began to protest, but the guards were deaf to your pleas. The dragged you into the elevator, ignoring your attempts to break free, descended to the first level, stuffed you into your ship, which stood alone in the empty hangar. Then they wished you bon voyage.

Of course, you could have incinerated them on the spot with the guns on your ship, but it seems the hangar was also furnished with a couple of stationary turrets that looked very persuasive.
loc.133.0:
You told the gaalian about the pirate plan to destroy the ranger, trying to smooth over the most sensitive parts so as to not make the old man nervous. When you finished, he was covered with some sort of suspicious yellow spots.
"This is just awful..." he whispered. "We've got to tell Major Ugrom about this quickly! It was right for you to go straight to him, young man. This is something for him to handle."
He contacted the major, who immediately arrived in the company of two henchmen. They searched you and the major picked the pistol up from the floor and began to examine it.
"He's clean," reported the guard who had searched you.
"Find out whose this is," said the major, throwing the pistol to him. "And don't let anybody come in here for twenty minutes. You're also dismissed," he said, moving his eyes to the second guard.

When just the two of you remained, the major ordered you to repeat what you had told the gaalian and began to listen intently, asking clarifying questions from time to time. 
"This is just awful, Urgom..." mumbled the gaalian when you had finished.
"Yes, sir. It would have been awful," the maloq answered gravely. "But it didn't happen. I propose we do the following: You contact all the major news agencies in our system and release a urgent statement saying that the hospital suffered a terrorist attack, but don't provide any details. And I'll use my channels to leak that all of the patients died in the terrorist attack. Then the relatives of our patients won't find out, but the news will be flying around pirate channels in less than a day. That way," he said, returning to you, "the pirates will be fooled and you won't have any trouble."
"That works for me!" you answered.
"Thank you, thank you so much!" said the gaalian as he ran up to you and began shaking your hand. "You've saved my life's work!"
You hesitated and the maloq was watching this scene with great skepticism, so you carefully freed your hand, wished everyone well, and headed toward the exit, not at all feeling like a hero.

The office was an enormous round dome made of glass framed in strips of plastic. The transparent walls open to a stunning view of mountain peaks capped with snow. In large vats that stand along the edges of the office, fantastic tropical plants grow, seemingly laughing at the cold on the other side of the glass.
Distracted by your study of the surrounding view, you entirely lost sight of the fact that the hospital chief was somewhere in the office - and probably very surprised by your sudden appearance, gun in hand.
You deafening shot rang out and a red spot began spreading from the center of your chest. You trembled and fell onto a luxurious shaggy carpet, staining it with your blood.
